messages.subject: Formatting data for mark-recapture distance sampling
parts:
Dear list members,

The answer to my question is probably very obvious, but I was wondering h=
ow to deal=20
with duplicates (otherwise called recaptures) when formatting data for im=
port into=20
distance and analysis with the MRDS engine.

I have a set of aerial observations of humpback whales obtained by two su=
rveyors=20
working independently on the same side of an aircraft, and I have identif=
ied a certain=20
number of duplicate sightings (by applying a set of rules I found in the =
literature).=20

In my database, I have created the three additional fields required by th=
e MRDS engine,=20
namely "Object", "Observer", and "Detected".=20

However, when two sightings a and b are regarded as being of the same ani=
mal (i.e.=20
recapture), should they both appear in the data or should only one be kep=
t and the other=20
one thrown out ? In practical terms, I'd like to know whether I should ha=
ve the following=20
structure : a,a and b,b or just a,a or b,b (as two lines per object are m=
andatory).=20

I am thinking that if I keep both observations, I will be overestimating =
the number of=20
recaptures, making Distance believe that a and b are actually different a=
nimals that were=20
seen by both observers. If that is correct, I am unsure nonetheless how t=
o decide which=20
sighting I should discard or retain. The problem is that due to the speed=
of the plane, the=20
visibility constraints inherent to these types of surveys, and the potent=
ial for=20
measurement errors, even though the sightings are fairly close together, =
the distances I=20
calculated based on recorded angles to the whales do differ.=20
Since detection functions are involved in the analysis of MRDS data, I wa=
s thinking that=20
choosing one sighting over the other might hence affect the histogram ret=
urned by the=20
software and the associated statistics I am interested in.

Hoping this is clear,

Many thanks in advance for your suggestions,

Phil

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Formatting data for mark-recapture distance sampling
parts:
Good morning Phil.

Have a look at the golf tees sample dataset that comes with Distance.
It will show you that indeed two records are needed for each detected
whale (one record for observer 1, second record for observer 2). There
will be the 'detected' field to indicate whether an observer saw the
whale (or golf tee). When detections are duplicates, there are 1s for
both observers.

So enter information for all whales ('objects' in Distance lingo) and
both observers (using 0/1 in the 'detected' field). The MRDS engine
will sort out the information you provide; no need to worry about
discarding or retaining information. Sound OK?
